## HabitToll vs ScreenZen

https://habittoll.com/compare/screenzen/ · German: https://habittoll.com/de/vergleich/screenzen/ · Spanish: https://habittoll.com/es/comparar/screenzen/

[Comparison](https://habittoll.com/compare/) · Updated 17 October 2026

Both slow you down before distracting apps, on iPhone and Android. ScreenZen makes you wait a few seconds before an app opens, can limit how often you open it, and is free, supported by optional tips; HabitToll asks “worth it?” each time and lets you buy 10 minutes at a price you set, or walk away for free.

### At a glance

|  | ScreenZen | HabitToll |
|----|----|----|
| What it is | A blocker for apps and websites that makes you wait before an app opens, with open limits, schedules and a daily screen-time budget | An app blocker that asks “worth it?” before the apps you pick open |
| Price | Free; optional tips from $5 to $40 on the US App Store, no subscription | Free to download, no subscription; 10-minute unlocks at a price you set, from €0.29 |
| When you open a limited app | A short wait, which can get longer each time; then you choose, and it opens for a set time | “Worth it?”: walk away for free, or buy 10 minutes |
| Getting past it | Wait it out; open limits and strict blocks can stop opens altogether; the settings can be locked, with a friend who can let you back in | Pay your price; 2 free emergency unlocks a month |
| Platforms | iPhone and iPad (iOS 16.4 or later), Mac, Android (8 or later), and Windows from its website | iPhone (iOS 26.4 or later) and Android (8 or later) |
| Account | Not needed for the main app | None |
| App Store privacy label | Data not linked to you: usage data and diagnostics, for analytics | Data linked to you: purchase history and a user ID, for the app’s features. Nothing used to track you |

### The main difference

ScreenZen slows you down with time: a wait before the app opens, which can grow with every open, short unlock sessions, and a limit on how many times a day an app opens. It does a lot for a free app: schedules, a daily screen-time budget, streaks, and a “Minimal” mode for apps like Instagram without Reels.

HabitToll slows you down with a price. Each time you open an app you picked, it asks “worth it?”, outside any free minutes or free hours you set. Walking away is one tap, free and counted; going in costs 10 minutes at a price you chose, then it asks again. One asks for a few seconds, the other for a small amount you decide on.

### When ScreenZen is the better fit

- You want a free blocker, and a wait is enough for you.
- You want a limit on how many times a day an app opens.
- You want it on an iPad, a Mac or Windows too.

### When HabitToll is the better fit

- You’d rather decide with a small price than wait it out.
- You want every walk-away counted, with a streak and a monthly bill.
- You want a settings lock where easier changes wait 24 hours or need a partner’s code.

### Questions

#### Is ScreenZen really free?

Yes. On 17 October 2026 the App Store and Google Play list it as free, with optional tips and no subscription. HabitToll is free to download too; you pay only when you buy 10 minutes of an app.

#### Is there a ScreenZen alternative with a price instead of a wait?

HabitToll. Before an app you picked opens, it asks “worth it?”; walking away is free, and 10 minutes cost a price you set, from €0.29, with no subscription.

*Facts checked on 17 October 2026 on the App Store (US and Germany), Google Play and screenzen.co. Prices change and differ by country. HabitToll is our app, so we’re not neutral; if something here is out of date, write to help@habittoll.com.*

## HabitToll vs Brick

https://habittoll.com/compare/brick/ · German: https://habittoll.com/de/vergleich/brick/ · Spanish: https://habittoll.com/es/comparar/brick/

[Comparison](https://habittoll.com/compare/) · Updated 17 October 2026

Brick is a small block you keep somewhere, like at home: tap your phone on it to block the apps you chose, and tap it again to unblock them, so getting back in means going to the Brick. HabitToll needs no device: it asks “worth it?” each time and lets you buy 10 minutes at a price you set, or walk away for free.

### At a glance

|  | Brick | HabitToll |
|----|----|----|
| What it is | A physical NFC block with an app: tap to block chosen apps and websites, tap again to unblock | An app blocker that asks “worth it?” before the apps you pick open |
| Price | $59 for the Brick (€63.95 in Germany, VAT included); the app is free, no subscription | Free to download, no subscription; 10-minute unlocks at a price you set, from €0.29 |
| When you open a blocked app | It stays blocked until you tap a Brick again | “Worth it?”: walk away for free, or buy 10 minutes |
| Getting past it | Go back to the Brick, or use one of 5 Emergency Unbricks (more on request) | Pay your price; 2 free emergency unlocks a month |
| Platforms | iPhone (iOS 18 or later) and Android (12 or later, with NFC); not iPad or Mac | iPhone (iOS 26.4 or later) and Android (8 or later) |
| Account | Needed | None |
| App Store privacy label | Data linked to you: email, user content, a user ID, usage data and diagnostics. Nothing used to track you | Data linked to you: purchase history and a user ID, for the app’s features. Nothing used to track you |

### The main difference

Brick makes getting back in a walk: the block stays in one place, and only tapping it unblocks your apps. That suits whole stretches of time, like an evening or a morning of work, for people who want a hard stop they set once.

HabitToll decides at each open instead. There’s no device to buy, carry or leave behind: the question comes up every time you open an app you picked, walking away is free and counted, and going in costs 10 minutes at your price, then it asks again.

### When Brick is the better fit

- You want your apps blocked for whole stretches, like evenings, and unblocked only at one place.
- You like a physical object to start and end focus time.
- You don’t mind paying once for the device.

### When HabitToll is the better fit

- You want a choice at each open, not a block until you’re back home.
- You don’t want to buy or carry a device.
- You want every walk-away counted, with a streak and a monthly bill.

### Questions

#### What happens if I lose my Brick?

Brick’s FAQ points to the 5 Emergency Unbricks, and any Brick works with any phone. Its lifetime guarantee replaces a Brick that stops working; we found no promise about a lost one. HabitToll has nothing to lose: it’s just the app.

#### Is there a Brick alternative without a device?

HabitToll: no device and no subscription. It asks “worth it?” before the apps you pick open; walking away is free, and 10 minutes cost a price you set, from €0.29.

*Facts checked on 17 October 2026 on the App Store (US and Germany), Google Play and getbrick.com, with its shop, FAQ and support pages. Prices change and differ by country. HabitToll is our app, so we’re not neutral; if something here is out of date, write to help@habittoll.com.*

## HabitToll Privacy Policy

https://habittoll.com/privacy/ · German: https://habittoll.com/de/datenschutz/ · Spanish: https://habittoll.com/es/privacidad/

*Last updated: 21 October 2026*

HabitToll puts a price on the apps you want to open less. This policy explains what data the app uses, where it goes and what you can do about it.

**The short version**

- Which apps you block, and how long you use them, are never sent to us. Device backups may contain a copy (see “Android and this version”).
- There’s no account. We never ask for your name, email, Apple Account or Google Account.
- **The app sends us nothing, except for Friends if you turn it on** (section 6). Your purchases go through Apple or Google Play.
- Purchase records and optional usage statistics (sections 4, 5 and 7) are not switched on yet. We’ll tell you in the app before either starts.
- We don’t sell data, don’t show ads in the app and don’t track you across other apps or websites.
- We may advertise HabitToll on platforms such as Apple, Google or Meta. The app and this website contain no advertising or tracking code, and this website sets no cookies (sections 14 and 15).

### Android and this version

This policy covers HabitToll on iPhone and Android. From version 1.0.3 on iPhone and 1.0.2 on Android, Friends (section 6) works when you turn it on, and its server logs (section 8) apply. Purchase records and usage statistics (sections 4, 5 and 7) are still not sent to our servers: those server features are not enabled. We will tell you before a later version enables them.

**What Android uses.** You enable usage access and permission to display over other apps during setup. While blocking is on and your screen is on, usage access lets HabitToll identify the app in front. Permission to display over other apps lets it show the pause screen over an app you chose to limit. The package names of the apps you select, such as `com.instagram.android`, stay on your phone. We do not receive your usage history or the identities of the apps you block. During setup, “Your last 7 days.” reads your daily usage for the preceding seven days and calculates an average on your phone. That calculation is not saved or sent. From version 1.0.5 on Android, HabitToll also keeps, on your phone, how long you use each app you picked each day, and your average for the week before you started, for your statistics. It is never sent and is left out of device backups. A persistent notification tells you when HabitToll is guarding your apps.

**Purchases and refunds.** On Android, a 10-minute pass is purchased through Google Play. Google handles payment and refunds under [Google’s privacy policy](https://policies.google.com/privacy). We do not receive your card details or Google Account details from the app. The app does not send Google Play its installation ID. The app stores its purchase records locally and sends none to our servers in this version. Refund requests go through [Google Play](https://support.google.com/googleplay/answer/2479637). The iPhone option “Confirm delivery to Apple” does not apply on Android. Google is responsible for the data it handles in Google Play and its backup service under its own policy.

**Device backups.** Your phone’s backup may contain HabitToll’s settings, history, streak and hashed partner code. Android permits Google device backup and transfer to a new device; iPhone backups may include app data in iCloud or a computer backup. The backup provider may hold a copy outside your phone; we never receive it. Uninstalling removes the app’s local files, but does not necessarily remove an existing device backup. Manage those copies through your backup provider.

There is no HabitToll account on either platform. We do not ask for your name, email, Apple Account or Google Account. Sections describing Apple’s Screen Time, purchases and delivery confirmation apply to the iPhone app; the Android details above apply instead on Android.

### 1. Who we are

The controller responsible for your data is:

Comads OÜ\
Ahtri tn 12, 15551 Tallinn, Estonia\
Registry code: 17276947\
Email: help@habittoll.com

We haven’t appointed a data protection officer; the law doesn’t require one for us. For anything about your data, write to help@habittoll.com.

### 2. What stays on your phone

The app does its work on your phone. These things are stored only there, and we never receive them:

- the apps you block, and on iPhone also websites. On iPhone, Apple gives the app only coded tokens, and iOS itself draws their names and icons; on Android, the app keeps the package names of the apps you pick (see “Android and this version”);
- when and how long you use them, every block screen you see and every time you walk away;
- your settings: price, monthly limit, free minutes and free hours, block times, the settings lock and the partner code;
- your answers during setup, such as your daily phone time and age range;
- your history, your monthly bill and your streak;
- the names you give your friends in the app.

The one exception is Friends, if you turn it on: then what your friends see goes to our server (section 6), that is, per day, how many unlocks you paid for and how much, and your streak. Never which apps.

On iPhone, the app uses Apple’s Screen Time framework to block apps; on Android, it uses usage access and permission to display over other apps. We don’t send any of this information anywhere.

Reminders, such as when an unlock is about to run out, are scheduled on your phone. We don’t send push notifications.

“Delete my data” (Settings → Your data) erases your history and setup answers on the phone. Deleting the app erases everything it stored on your phone; a device backup may still hold a copy (see “Android and this version”).

### 3. A random ID instead of an account

When you first open the app, it creates a random ID for this installation (the “install ID”). It isn’t linked to your name, email, phone number, Apple Account or device. We use it:

- to match purchases to this installation. Apple stores it with each purchase (as the “app account token”);
- for usage statistics, only if you choose to share them (section 7);
- as your support ID. The first 8 characters are shown in Help, so we can find your data when you write to us.

Friends uses a separate random ID (section 6), so friends data is never joined with your purchases or statistics.

### 4. Purchases

You buy unlocks from Apple, through Apple’s purchase sheet. Apple handles the payment. We never see your card or payment details, your name or your Apple Account. Apple’s privacy policy applies to that part: [apple.com/legal/privacy](https://www.apple.com/legal/privacy/).

When a paid unlock starts, the app sends our server:

- the install ID;
- Apple’s signed record of the purchase: transaction ID, product (price tier), price and currency, purchase date, App Store country, and whether it was a test purchase;
- the app version and platform;
- your answers to the two consent questions (usage statistics, section 7; delivery confirmation, section 5), with a counter that keeps the answers in the right order.

Our server also records when it first and last heard from the installation.

Apple also informs our server about purchases and refunds (App Store Server Notifications). For example, it tells us that a purchase happened, that a refund was requested and the reason given to Apple, and Apple’s decision.

- **Why:** to deliver what you paid for, to handle refunds correctly, to prevent misuse and to know how often refunds happen.
- **Legal basis:**
  - our contract with you (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR);
  - our legitimate interest in correct refunds and in preventing misuse (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR);
  - legal record-keeping duties (Art. 6(1)(c) GDPR).
- **How long:** 24 months after the purchase, then deleted, unless a law requires us to keep a record longer.

### 5. Refunds: “Confirm delivery to Apple” (off unless you switch it on)

If you ask Apple for a refund, Apple may ask us whether the unlock was delivered. **We answer only if you switched on “Confirm delivery to Apple”** in Settings → Your data. It’s off until you switch it on, and the app never asks you to.

If it’s on, we tell Apple about that purchase:

- that you consented;
- that the unlock was delivered, but only if the app reported that it was;
- that the pay screen showed what the purchase does and its price before you bought it.

We never tell Apple how many minutes you used. We don’t know.

- **Legal basis:** your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR).
- **Withdrawing:** switch it off at any time. We then stop answering for future requests.
- **If it’s off:** we don’t answer, and Apple decides alone.

### 6. Friends (optional)

Friends stays off until you turn it on and invite someone, or accept someone’s invite.

**What your friends see, per day:**

- how many unlocks you paid for, and how much. You can hide the amounts with “Show amounts”;
- your streak (days without a paid unlock) and your best, which you can hide with “Show streak”.

They never see which apps, what time or for how long. They also never see your walk-aways, your free or emergency unlocks, or your settings.

**What our server stores for Friends:**

- a random friend ID and a scrambled (hashed) form of its secret key. The key itself stays on your phone;
- the daily numbers above, for the last 35 days, and your streak and best;
- who is linked with whom, and the people you blocked;
- open invite codes, stored only in a scrambled form;
- cheers (a stamp, no text), for 30 days;
- your platform, your three Friends switches and when your profile was last used.

**Preventing abuse:** we count requests to stop invite codes from being guessed. For a few kinds of request, we count per IP address using a one-way scrambled form that changes every day, and we delete these counters within about two hours. We never store your IP address itself in our database.

- **Why:** to show your progress to the friends you chose, as you asked.
- **Legal basis:**
  - our contract with you (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR);
  - for the abuse counters, our legitimate interest in keeping the service safe (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
- **How long:**
  - daily numbers: 35 days;
  - invites: 30 days after they were used or expired;
  - cheers: 30 days.
- **Deleting:** “Turn off Friends” or “Delete my data” deletes your friends profile, and everything linked to it on our server, at once. A profile is also deleted automatically:
  - 30 days after its last use, if it has no friends and no open invites;
  - 12 months after its last use in any case.

Only people you invited, or whose invite you accepted, see your numbers. You can remove or block a friend at any time.

### 7. Usage statistics (only if you tap “Share”)

The app asks you once whether to share usage statistics. **Until you tap “Share”, nothing is recorded for statistics.**

If you share, the app sends events such as:

- setup steps completed;
- a purchase started, completed or cancelled, with its price and currency;
- the monthly limit reached, or a streak milestone;
- your answers to short questions in the app, for example why you stopped blocking;
- your rough daily phone time from setup, as a range;
- once a day, a summary with rough counts, such as “3–5”.

Each event carries the install ID, the app version and when it happened. Statistics never contain which apps you block, app names, how long you used them or anything you type.

- **Why:** to understand what helps and what doesn’t, and to improve the app.
- **Legal basis:** your consent (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR). Keeping the events on your device until they’re sent also needs your consent under the ePrivacy rules of your country (in Germany, § 25 TDDDG).
- **Provider:** PostHog Inc., in its EU cloud (Frankfurt, Germany).
  - We don’t use PostHog’s app library. The app sends one small request itself: no device identifiers, no automatic tracking, no screen recording, and location lookup switched off.
  - As with any connection, PostHog sees the IP address the request comes from. We’ve set PostHog not to store it.
- **Refunds:** if you share statistics, our server also tells PostHog when a purchase of yours is refunded (install ID, product, price and currency). This measures how often refunds happen.
- **How long:** 12 months, then deleted.
- **Withdrawing:** Settings → Your data → Usage stats. From then on nothing is sent, events not yet sent are deleted, and the app tells our server to stop the refund events.

### 8. Server logs

When the app talks to our server, the server keeps short technical logs, for example the time, the function called and errors. Connection errors can include an IP address. We use them to run the service and fix errors. Our logs never contain your install ID, friend ID or keys.

- **Legal basis:** our legitimate interest in a working, secure service (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
- **How long:** 14 days.

### 9. Who handles data for us

- **Amazon Web Services EMEA SARL** (Luxembourg) hosts our server and database in the EU (Frankfurt, Germany).
- **PostHog Inc.** stores usage statistics in its EU cloud (Frankfurt, Germany), and only if you share them.
- **Cloudflare Inc.** forwards email sent to help@habittoll.com (section 13).
- **GitHub Inc.** hosts this website (section 15).
- **Apple** runs the App Store, payments and refunds. Apple is responsible for that data itself, under its own privacy policy.

AWS, PostHog and Cloudflare work only on our instructions, under data processing agreements, and must protect the data at least as well as this policy describes. PostHog and Cloudflare are US companies, and AWS belongs to the US company Amazon. If data is accessed from outside the EU, the European Commission’s standard contractual clauses or the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework protect it.

### 10. Your rights

You have the right to:

- get a copy of your data (Art. 15 GDPR), and receive it in a machine-readable format (Art. 20);
- have it corrected (Art. 16);
- have it deleted (Art. 17), or its use restricted (Art. 18);
- object to uses based on our legitimate interests (Art. 21);
- withdraw any consent at any time (Art. 7(3)). This doesn’t affect what happened before you withdrew;
- complain to a data protection authority. That can be the Estonian Data Protection Inspectorate (Andmekaitse Inspektsioon, Tatari 39, 10134 Tallinn, [www.aki.ee](https://www.aki.ee)), or the authority where you live or work.

**How to use them.** In the app, go to Settings → Your data:

- “Delete my data” erases your history and setup answers on the phone, and your friends data on our server.
- “Ask for a copy or erasure” opens an email to us with your support ID, so we can find your purchase records. We answer within one month.

We don’t know who you are, so we can only find your data through the IDs the app holds. Please send requests from the app.

### 11. Age

HabitToll is for adults (18+). It isn’t meant for children, and we don’t knowingly collect data from children.

### 12. Backups

Deleted data can remain in our hosting provider’s backups until those backups are replaced, for at most 30 days.

### 13. Emailing us

If you write to us, we receive your email address, your message and anything you attach. Mail sent to help@habittoll.com is forwarded by Cloudflare (Cloudflare Email Routing) to the mailbox we answer from, at Google (Gmail). We use your message only to answer you and to settle your request.

- **Legal basis:** our contract with you, when you write about the app or a purchase (Art. 6(1)(b) GDPR); otherwise our legitimate interest in answering you (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).
- **How long:** until your request is settled, and at most 24 months, unless the law requires us to keep it longer.

### 14. Advertising for HabitToll

The app shows no ads. Neither the app nor this website contains advertising or tracking code.

We may advertise HabitToll on other services, for example Apple (ads on the App Store), Google (such as Search and YouTube), Meta (Facebook, Instagram) or TikTok. Those ads are shown by the platform under its own privacy policy, and the platform decides, as its own controller, which of your data it uses to show them. From the platforms we receive only overall numbers, such as how many people saw an ad or downloaded the app. They don’t tell us who you are.

If we ever want to measure our ads with tools in the app or on this website, for example from Apple, Google or Meta, we’ll first add them to this policy. Where the law requires consent, we’ll ask for it before anything is read from or stored on your device: in the app with Apple’s “Allow tracking” prompt or our own question, on this website with a clear choice to accept or decline.

### 15. This website

These pages are hosted on GitHub Pages by GitHub, Inc. (USA). Like any web host, GitHub records the IP address of visitors to keep the service secure; see [GitHub’s Privacy Statement](https://docs.github.com/site-policy/privacy-policies/github-general-privacy-statement). The domain habittoll.com is registered with Cloudflare, Inc., which only points it to GitHub; your visits don’t pass through Cloudflare.

**No cookies, no tracking.** This website sets no cookies and stores nothing in your browser. It uses no analytics, tracking or advertising code, and loads nothing from other companies; even its fonts come from these pages. That’s why there’s no cookie banner. If we ever add cookies or similar technology that isn’t strictly necessary, we’ll ask for your consent first (Art. 6(1)(a) GDPR; in Germany § 25 TDDDG).

- **Legal basis:** our legitimate interest in providing these pages safely (Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR).

### 16. Changes

If we change this policy, we’ll update the date at the top. If a change matters to you, we’ll also tell you in the app.

## HabitToll Terms of Use

https://habittoll.com/terms/ · German: https://habittoll.com/de/nutzungsbedingungen/ · Spanish: https://habittoll.com/es/condiciones/

*Last updated: 16 October 2026*

These terms are the agreement between you and Comads OÜ (“we”, details in section 15) for the HabitToll app on iPhone and Android. They’re short; please read them.

### 1. What HabitToll is

HabitToll blocks the apps you want to use less: on iPhone with Apple’s Screen Time, on Android with Android’s own permissions (section 12). When you open a blocked app, a block screen appears. You can:

- walk away (“Not worth it”);
- use one of the free ways through (section 4); or
- buy a 10-minute unlock at a price you chose yourself.

Blocking, your statistics, the monthly bill, streaks and Friends cost nothing. There’s no subscription.

HabitToll is a self-control tool. It isn’t a medical product or a treatment, and we can’t promise any particular result.

### 2. Who can use it

You must be at least 18. You use HabitToll on your own device, for yourself. Don’t use it to control someone else’s device.

### 3. Unlocks you pay for

- **You set the rules.** During setup and in Settings, you choose:
  - your price per unlock;
  - whether the price doubles for each further unlock the same day. It goes up to at most 10× your price, and resets at 04:00;
  - a monthly limit. Prices above €19.99 need one.
- **What one unlock is:** a one-time in-app purchase, a “10-minute pass”. It opens the app you tapped for 10 minutes of use. It starts right away, and ends after 10 minutes of use or 60 minutes after it started, whichever comes first. Unused minutes don’t carry over.
- **You buy it from Apple.** Every payment goes through Apple’s purchase sheet, at the price Apple shows there, under Apple’s Media Services Terms. Apple charges you and handles the payment.
- **The price before you pay:** the block screen and the pay screen show the price of this unlock, and of the next one, before Apple’s sheet opens.
- **Your monthly limit:**
  - Past your limit, the app asks before every paid unlock.
  - With “Stop at my limit” on, paid unlocks stop until the 1st of the next month. Emergency unlocks still work.
  - A purchase you already confirmed on Apple’s sheet, or one waiting for approval, is always delivered when it completes.
- **If a purchase completes later**, for example after an approval, HabitToll delivers it as soon as Apple passes it on, usually the next time you open HabitToll. If it’s the only request at that price from the last 24 hours and its app is still blocked, that app opens for 10 minutes then. Otherwise it’s kept as a prepaid unlock and used for your next unlock.
- **If iOS locks a paid unlock again too early**, less than 9 minutes after it started (sooner than its 10 minutes could have been used), your next unlock is free. An unlock that ends at the 60-minute limit isn’t made up. If anything else went wrong with an unlock you paid for, write to us, or ask Apple for a refund.
- **Refunds** are decided by Apple. You can ask Apple at [reportaproblem.apple.com](https://reportaproblem.apple.com), or through Help → Refunds in the app. Your legal rights as a consumer are not affected.

### 4. Free ways through

- “Not worth it” is always one tap, and always free.
- Depending on your settings, you also have:
  - free minutes each day, one pass shared by all your apps;
  - 2 free emergency unlocks a month (10 minutes each). They also work when your monthly limit is reached;
  - free make-up unlocks (section 3).
- You can remove apps, lower your price or stop blocking in Settings. If you turned on the settings lock, these changes wait 24 hours or need your partner’s code.
- Switching off Screen Time access for HabitToll in the iPhone’s Settings, or deleting the app, always ends blocking.

### 5. The settings lock

If you turn on the settings lock, changes that make blocking easier wait 24 hours, or need the code of a person you chose. This is your own choice, for your own benefit. It never affects the free ways through in section 4.

### 6. Friends

If you use Friends, the people you invite (or whose invite you accept) see:

- how many unlocks you paid for each day, and how much, unless you hide the amounts;
- your streak, unless you hide it.

They never see which apps. Friends can’t change your settings.

Invite only people you know. Don’t try to guess invite codes, send floods of invites or misuse Friends in any other way. If someone does, we may remove their Friends profile.

### 7. Fair use

Don’t copy, resell, reverse-engineer or tamper with the app, its purchases or our servers, except where the law allows it.

### 8. Availability and changes

HabitToll depends on Apple’s Screen Time, which we don’t control. We work to keep the app reliable, but we can’t promise it will always work without errors or interruptions.

We may improve and change the app. If a change affects an unlock you’ve paid for and not yet used, we’ll deliver it, or you can ask Apple for a refund.

### 9. Liability

We’re liable without limit:

- for damage we cause intentionally or through gross negligence;
- for injury to life, body or health;
- wherever the law doesn’t allow a limit.

For damage caused by slight negligence, we’re liable only if we breach a duty that’s essential to this agreement, and only for the typical damage that could be foreseen. Otherwise, as far as the law allows, we’re not liable.

### 10. Ending

You can stop at any time by deleting the app. Before you do, Settings → Your data lets you delete your data.

### 11. Apple

- Your licence to use the app is Apple’s standard [Licensed Application End User License Agreement](https://www.apple.com/legal/internet-services/itunes/dev/stdeula/). These terms add the rules for HabitToll’s features and purchases.
- These terms are between you and us, not Apple. We, not Apple, are responsible for the app, its support and any claims about it.
- Apple and its subsidiaries are third-party beneficiaries of these terms, and may enforce them against you.

### 12. Android and Google Play

On Android, these terms apply in the same way, with these differences:

- **Blocking** uses two permissions you turn on during setup: usage access, to see which app is in front, and display over other apps, to show the block screen. HabitToll depends on them and on Android, which we don’t control, just as section 8 says for Apple’s Screen Time. Turning either permission off for HabitToll in Android’s Settings, or uninstalling the app, always ends blocking.
- **You buy it from Google Play.** Every payment goes through Google Play’s purchase sheet, at the price Google Play shows there, under the [Google Play Terms of Service](https://play.google.com/about/play-terms/). Google charges you and handles the payment. What sections 3 and 8 say about Apple applies here to Google Play.
- **An unlock counts only the time its app is in front.** The make-up rule in section 3 (“If iOS locks a paid unlock again too early”) is for iPhone only.
- **Refunds** are decided by Google Play. You can ask in your [Google Play order history](https://play.google.com/store/account/orderhistory), or through Help → Refunds in the app. Your legal rights as a consumer are not affected.
- **Section 11 is for iPhone only.** On Android, these terms are between you and us, not Google. We, not Google, are responsible for the app, its support and any claims about it.

### 13. Changes to these terms

We may update these terms, for example when the app or the law changes. We’ll tell you in the app before an important change takes effect. If you don’t agree, you can stop using the app.

### 14. Law and disputes

Estonian law applies. If you’re a consumer, you keep the protection of the mandatory laws of the country where you live, and you can bring a claim before its courts.

### VAT

Comads OÜ isn’t registered for value-added tax and has no VAT identification number (small-business status under Estonian law).

### Consumer dispute resolution

We are neither obliged nor willing to take part in dispute resolution proceedings before a consumer arbitration board.
